text:
simon: Heads-up — perf regression observed when running TP x8 with mixed precision (FP8 path + INT8 quantized kernels). Throughput drops ~18% compared to last week. Profiling attached.

anna: saw this on staging too, started after the kernel selector tweak yesterday. :thinking:

jeff: quick note from the profiler: kernel_selector is choosing `matmul_fused_v2` for sequence lengths > 512, but that path uses a non-shared workspace which causes extra memcpy on TP shards. Timeline shows compute stalls waiting on DMA.

simon: relevant trace excerpt:```
[GPU0] 0.0ms - launch matmul_fused_v2 (s=1024)
[GPU0] 0.8ms - async memcpy H2D workspace
[GPU0] 1.6ms - waiting on NCCL allreduce (delta=0.9ms)
[GPU0] 2.5ms - compute resume
```

rachel: also seeing KV-cache churn on the same traces. On TP shard boundary the prefix cache misses and we end up re-loading KV across NCCL frequently. Logs:```
KVCache: miss seq=256 shard=3 -> fetch remote (size=24MB)
KVCache: insert seq=256 shard=3 (evicted seq=128 shard=3)
```

jeff: that eviction pattern is suspicious — looks like our shard placement + cache size heuristic doesn't account for TP steady-state access pattern. Batching heuristics exacerbate it: we pack many short contexts into a single batch so different requests map to different shards and thrash the KV allocator.

simon: interestingly, when I forced kernel_selector to `matmul_tiled` the memcpy goes away and throughput recovers ~12% (not full but better). Command I used: `export RW_KERNEL_HINT=matmul_tiled && ./bench --tp 8 --fp8`

anna: can you drop the perf trace link here? I'll run the same with nvprof and NCCL tracing on my machine.

simon: trace: https://perf.redwood/internal/traces/1769123456-tp-fp8-kv (internal)

perf-bot: perf-alert: TP-FP8 throughput drop (p95 latency up 22%) — alerted 5 engineers.

jeff: hypothesis list: 1) kernel selection picks a kernel with extra workspace memcpys that serialize with NCCL, 2) KV cache eviction policy too-aggressive for TP shard patterns, 3) quantized matmul numeric fallback path triggers slower kernels under certain sequence lengths.

rachel: small repro plan:
- pin kernel selector to `matmul_tiled` vs `matmul_fused_v2`
- run with KV cache size x2 and x0.5 to see thrash pattern
- enable NCCL_TRACE=1 and collect timeline
- compare FP8 vs INT8 codepath (quantized kernels)

simon: I'll create a minimal repro harness and run on 8xA100; will post results here. ETA ~2hrs.

anna: I'll try the same on DGX cluster, can also try an FP16-only run to isolate FP8/quantization interaction.

jeff: note — we recently landed a micro-optimization that changes GEMM tile shape for FP8 to reduce register pressure. Maybe that inadvertently increased global memory traffic on certain sizes. Filing an issue now.

simon: filed issue: https://issues.redwood/INF-1428 (kernel-selector + KV thrash + TP)

rachel: temporary mitigation for prod: add routing rule to prefer dedicated nodes for TP+FP8 workloads, and fallback to FP16 when host header `X-Allow-FP8=false`. Should limit customer impact.

perf-bot: action-item created: INF-1428 assigned to jeff, simon, rachel — due EOD.

jeff: next steps: I'll try reproducer + compare kernels, simon/rachel run KV cache experiments, anna run NCCL timelines. Sync in 3hrs here. :thumbsup:
